prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now needs a bearer key and checks its role, and requests that change data are written to an audit log that GET /audit returns (managers only). npm test (26 tests) and npm run lint both pass. I checked the role rules with a one-off script that I did not keep, and added no new tests. Missing or unknown keys get 401 `unauthorized` and known keys without permission get 403 `forbidden`. A cook may only cook, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts, so starting or finishing a stock-take is for managers. The audit records every request other than a read (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) made with a known key, including refused or failed ones; requests with no key or an unknown key are not recorded. The schema version stays at 2 because the new apiKeys and audit lists are optional. data/db.json, the file `npm start` uses, has no keys yet, so the running server will turn every request away until keys are added there. The existing tests send the manager key through tests/helpers.js.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
